translation_en: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali, Ibn Abi 'Umar, Muhammad ibn Rafi', and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us. The wording is Ibn Rafi''s. Ibn Rafi' and Ibn Abi 'Umar said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; the other two said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Abu Sufyan informed him. He said: During the period of truce between me and the Messenger of Allah, I went to Syria. While I was there, a letter from the Messenger of Allah was brought to Heraclius, the great ruler of the Romans. Dihyah al-Kalbi had brought it and handed it to the governor of Busra, who passed it to Heraclius. Heraclius asked: Is anyone here from the people of this man who claims to be a prophet? They said yes. I was summoned with a group of Quraysh. We entered upon Heraclius, and he seated us before him. He asked: Which of you is most closely related to this man who claims to be a prophet? Abu Sufyan said: I am the closest. They seated me in front of him and placed my companions behind me. Then he called for his interpreter and said: Tell them that I will question this man about the man who claims to be a prophet. If he lies to me, they must declare him a liar. Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, had I not feared that a lie would be reported about me, I would have lied. Then Heraclius told his interpreter to ask me about the man's lineage. I said: He is of noble lineage among us. Heraclius asked: Was any of his forefathers a king? I said no. He asked: Did you accuse him of lying before he made this claim? I said no. He asked: Do the nobles follow him or the weak? I said: The weak. He asked: Are they increasing or decreasing? I said: They are increasing. He asked: Does anyone leave his religion in anger after entering it? I said: No. He asked: Have you fought him? I said: Yes. He asked: How has the fighting between you and him gone? I said: The war between us has alternated; sometimes he has the upper hand over us and sometimes we have it over him. He asked: Does he betray? I said: No. We are in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it. By Allah, I could not find a way to insert anything against him except that answer. Heraclius asked: Has anyone made this claim before him? I said no. He told his interpreter to say: I asked you about his lineage, and you said he is of noble lineage among you. Such are the messengers: they are sent from the noble families of their people. I asked whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you said no. I said that if one of his forefathers had been a king, I would have thought he was seeking to reclaim his forefathers' kingdom. I asked whether his followers were weak people or nobles, and you said the weak. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether you accused him of lying before he made this claim, and you said no. I know, then, that he would not refrain from lying about people and then go and lie about Allah. I asked whether anyone leaves his religion in anger after entering it, and you said no. That is how faith is when its delight has entered the hearts. I asked whether his followers are increasing or decreasing, and you said they are increasing. That is how faith continues until it is complete. I asked whether you fought him, and you said you did, and that the war between you alternates, with him gaining advantage over you and you over him. Such is the case with messengers: they are tested, but the final outcome is theirs. I asked whether he betrays, and you said no. Such is the way of messengers: they do not betray. I asked whether anyone made this claim before him, and you said no. I said that if someone had made this claim before him, I would have thought he was repeating something said before. Then Heraclius asked: What does he command you to do? I said: He commands us to pray, give charity, maintain family ties, and remain chaste. He said: If what you say about him is true, then he is a prophet. I knew that a prophet would appear, but I did not think he would come from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would love to meet him. If I were with him, I would wash his feet. His dominion will surely reach beneath my feet. Then Heraclius called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah and read it. It said: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, great ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows the guidance. To proceed: I call you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe, and Allah will give you your reward twice over. If you turn away, the sin of the common people will be upon you. O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords besides Allah. If they turn away, say: Bear witness that we are Muslims. When Heraclius finished reading the letter, voices rose around him and there was much commotion. He ordered that we be taken out. As we left, I said to my companions: The affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become momentous. The king of the Byzantines fears him. I remained certain that the Messenger of Allah's cause would prevail, until Allah brought Islam to me.
